label: Church as a visible, enduring society…: The community described in Lumen gentium §8 as visibly…
term: Church as a visible, enduring society with authority
definition: The community described in Lumen gentium §8 as visibly constituted, continually sustained, equipped with hierarchical organs, entrusted to Peter and the apostles for pastoral government, and established in perpetuity. This is the visible/social aspect of the one complex Church of which the source also speaks spiritually; it is not a claim that the Church is exhausted by an external organization or that every later institutional detail was fixed at its inception.
note: This sense interprets VisibleWithAuthority in the stage-5 source reading, not every possible society in Signature. Source evidence for the reading does not establish its historical truth or supply stage-6 identity.

formal_gap.meaning: Signature.VisibleWithAuthority c says that the society c is visibly constituted, enduring and equipped with an authority structure for its government, as Lumen gentium §8 describes the Church's visible, social aspect. It is a supplied predicate on societies.
examples: A society with hierarchical organs and continuous government, such as the one stage 5 says Christ founded.
exclusions: An invisible communion alone, without visible organization.
The spiritual community of the Church (DEF-CHURCH-SPIRITUAL-COMMUNITY): a separate aspect that the source joins with this one without reducing either (DISAMB-CHURCH-VISIBLE-SPIRITUAL-ASPECTS).
A claim that every later institutional detail was fixed at the society's beginning.
open_obligations: Stage 5 (STMT-CHRIST-FOUNDED-VISIBLE-CHURCH) and stage 6 (STMT-CHRISTS-CHURCH-IS-THE-CATHOLIC-CHURCH) use it in open premises; source evidence for the reading does not establish their historical truth.
What counts as visibility, endurance and authority for arbitrary societies of the signature is not fixed in Lean.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
